newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NAB shares scramble to record high.
newsitem.headline: NAB shares scramble to record high.

text.p: Shares in Australia's largest bank National Australia Bank Ltd scrambled to a record high A$17.30 in a day of choppy trade on Monday as the stock remained the pick of the popular sector, brokers said.

Reasons for the sector leader's popularity were mixed, with the perennial dividend yield attraction of bank stocks cited, as were newspaper reports that the bank was ahead in the race to buy Axiom Funds Management, the manager of superannuation funds belonging to New South Wales public servants.

"NAB has led the way in the banks which have done relatively well. They have still got the yield that attracts the clients," said one dealer. However, others suggested that hopes for the bank's fund management arm had been the spark, citing newspaper articles that discussed the tenderers, NAB and German-owned financial giant, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"I can only put it down to the newspaper reports about Axiom you have seen today," said a Sydney-based broker.
NAB shares closed 11 cents higher at A$17.18 on options exercise boosted turnover of 27 million shares.
